questions.q: What does LRS (Locally Redundant Storage) actually keep?
options: Three synchronous copies of your data within a single datacenter
Three copies spread across different Azure regions
A single copy with no redundancy at all
Three copies across different Availability Zones
questions.explain: LRS keeps three copies in one datacenter — the cheapest option, protecting against drive/rack failure but not a datacenter-wide outage.

questions.q: What makes ZRS different from LRS?
options: ZRS spreads its three copies synchronously across separate Availability Zones in the same region, instead of one datacenter
ZRS keeps only one copy of the data
ZRS replicates data to a different Azure region entirely
ZRS is cheaper than LRS
questions.explain: ZRS protects against a single datacenter failure by spreading copies across Availability Zones within the region, at a modest cost increase over LRS.

questions.q: What does GRS protect against that ZRS cannot?
options: A regional disaster, because GRS asynchronously replicates a copy to a separate paired region
Hardware failure inside a single server rack
A single Availability Zone going offline
Nothing — GRS and ZRS provide identical protection
questions.explain: GRS replicates to Azure's designated paired region, hundreds of miles away, which survives a disaster that takes out an entire region — something ZRS can't do since it never leaves the region.

questions.q: What is a real tradeoff of choosing GRS over LRS or ZRS?
options: Higher cost (paying for storage in two regions) and asynchronous replication, so the most recent writes could theoretically be lost in a true regional failure
GRS has no downsides compared to LRS or ZRS
GRS is always the cheapest redundancy option
GRS cannot be used with StorageV2 accounts
questions.explain: GRS costs more because it pays for storage in two regions, and because replication is asynchronous, the very latest writes aren't guaranteed to have landed in the secondary region yet.

questions.q: What does a lifecycle management policy do?
options: Automatically moves or deletes blobs in a container based on how long since they were last modified
Automatically changes a storage account's redundancy option over time
Automatically resizes a Managed Disk attached to a VM
Automatically creates new storage accounts when one fills up
questions.explain: A lifecycle policy is a rule, defined once, that Azure evaluates continuously to tier or delete blobs by age — automating the manual tiering from Lesson 14.
